record.comparison: RGBAf of the unchanged final mask graph rendered to private 1024x1024 scratch in original absolute partition order (or full width x256 control). Four native RGBAf reads counted for each output using the same normalised linear MTL sampler on its respective physical scratch extent. Only 16-byte-per-pixel half-width/half-height output is held. Original four 1200x800 sRGB8 FIT windows reassembled, then all 15,360,000 bytes compared to the canonical display. Checked width/height are even. Every real arm also independently blits every half-plane byte in 64-row batches for SHA-256.
record.restrictions: The physical texture size, local normalised sampler, CI request shape, and cache-clearing cadence vary between arms. This study does not isolate the causal subdivision or prove which CI instruction caused a difference. It compares full native finite decisions and complete half-size RGBAf fingerprints. No preserved byte-for-byte full native RGBAf comparison between the real arms. CPU blit/hash contributes to the reported full transport clock, whereas halfWriteAndValidationMs ends at the last completed group check. Two states shared a process per role; do not interpret cumulative process high-water as separate arm peaks.
